message:
docs(history): the capture failure is not contention, and not RDP

I recorded that gdi_capture_process failed because the live host was capturing
the same screen. It was not. With GNLink stopped entirely and the console session
active, the verifier reproduced the failure twice, at 42.99 and 46.99 fps.

I then ran it under the same conditions and it PASSED at 56.67. Same machine,
same state, opposite verdicts -- so the suite wobbles around its 50 fps
threshold, and any single run of it decides very little.

The real signal is underneath the threshold. Copy time is the ceiling, not the
refresh rate: 1/copyAvg matches the measured fps to the decimal on both sides
(1/0.017644 = 56.7 for mine, 1/0.0233 = 42.9 for theirs). And the isolated
capture process takes 17-23 ms for a copy the parent does in 1.8-2.5 ms -- about
ten times slower, unexplained.

So it is recorded as unexplained and separate, not as environmental and therefore
ignorable. It reproduces with neither RDP nor GNLink in the picture, which means
CLAUDE.md's existing RDP exception does not cover it. On the task list below the
in-app update work.

The explanation I reached for first was plausible and checkable, and I did not
check it -- confirming it needed the live app stopped, which I am not allowed to
do. Leaving it unverified was right. What I missed is that the user stopped
GNLink themselves, and the condition I needed existed; the verifier is the one
who asked again. An item left unverified should be re-asked when the conditions
change.
